# Summary of the UK Independence Party Manifesto 2015

## Introduction and Vision

UKIP presents itself as a fundamentally different alternative to the establishment parties, offering voters a chance for real change in British politics. The manifesto is framed around the core belief that Britain is a proud, independent nation capable of governing itself without interference from the European Union. UKIP positions itself as the only party willing to restore sovereignty, control borders, and return power to the British people. The party claims its policies are fully costed and independently verified, unlike the "arbitrary, over-ambitious" pledges of other parties.

## Economic Policy

UKIP's economic approach centers on cutting taxes, eliminating the deficit, and leaving the EU. Key commitments include raising the personal allowance to £13,000, abolishing inheritance tax, and ensuring the minimum wage is tax-free. The party promises to fund these measures through savings from leaving the EU (£9 billion annually), reducing overseas aid, scrapping the HS2 rail project, and replacing the Barnett Formula. UKIP pledges fiscal responsibility while increasing spending on vital services.

## Immigration

Immigration is framed as a matter of space and sustainability, not race. UKIP blames uncontrolled EU migration for driving down wages, straining public services, and creating housing shortages. The solution lies in leaving the EU to regain border control and implementing an Australian-style points-based immigration system. This would treat all nationalities equally while prioritizing skilled workers needed by Britain's economy. A five-year moratorium on unskilled migration would allow existing residents to find work and wages to recover.

## NHS and Health

The NHS is described as Britain's "best-loved institution" now in crisis due to immigration pressures, EU directives, and political mismanagement. UKIP pledges £12 billion additional investment over five years, funding 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses, and improved mental health services. The party would end "health tourism" by requiring migrants to have medical insurance and contribute taxes for five years before accessing non-urgent NHS treatment. Hospital parking charges would be abolished.

## Social Issues

UKIP commits to protecting pensions, supporting carers with increased allowances, and reforming disability assessments by returning them to GPs rather than ATOS-style contractors. The "bedroom tax" would be scrapped. On education, the party supports grammar schools, vocational training, and abolishing tuition fees for STEMM subjects to address skills shortages.

## Brexit and Sovereignty

Leaving the EU is the central policy, described as essential for regaining control over laws, borders, and trade. UKIP dismisses fears about job losses as "myths" and argues Britain will thrive trading globally on its own terms. The party would repeal the Human Rights Act, withdraw from European Court jurisdiction, and introduce a British Bill of Rights.

## Conclusion

The manifesto presents a comprehensive vision of an independent Britain, free from EU "shackles," with restored sovereignty, controlled immigration, and renewed national pride. UKIP positions itself as the only party honest enough to address public concerns about immigration and EU membership while protecting cherished institutions like the NHS.
